 -versus-
 State of Odisha .... Respondent
Mr. C.K. Pradhan, Aga
Coram:
Justice Biraja Prasanna Satapathy

Order
07.11.2025 Order No. I.A. No.2273 of 2022
04. 1.
This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual/Physical) Mode.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
3. This application has been filed seeking grant of bail by keeping the sentence under suspension.

4. It is contended that basing on the allegation made in the FIR in Daspalla P.S. Case No.79 dated 02.07.2019, appellant faced the trial in the Court of learned C.J.M.-cum-Asst. Sessions Judge,
Nayagarh in S.T. Case No.64/227 of 2019 for the offence under Section-450/376(2)(1)(n) & 506 of IPC.

However, vide the impugned judgment, appellant was convicted and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 10 years and to pay a fine of Rs.5000/- in default to undergo six months R.I. and to undergo 2(two) months R.I. for the offence under Section 506 of IPC.
It is contended that petitioner was on pre-trial bail being allowed by this Court vide order dated 03.12.2019 in BLAPL No.9812 of 2019.
(Copy of the order so produced in Court be kept in record.)
4.2. It is however contended that after being convicted vide the impugned judgment, petitioner is in custody since 28.10.2022.

It is contended that since petitioner was on pre-trial bail being allowed by this Court and he never mis-utilized the liberty so granted and petitioner has already undergone more than 3 (three) years of the substantive sentence, petitioner be released on bail on such terms and conditions as deem fit and proper by keeping the sentence under suspension.

sentences.text: 5. Learned Addl.

Standing Counsel on the other hand while opposing the prayer for bail, contended that since appellant has not undergone as yet 50% of the sentence so imposed, Appellant's prayer for grant of regular bail is required to be rejected.

However, it is not disputed that the appellant was allowed pre-trial bail by this Court in BLAPL No.9812 of 2019 and he // 3 // remained on bail till convicted and sentenced vide the impugned jugment.

6. Having heard learned counsel for the parties, considering the submissions made and the fact that appellant was on bail during trial vide order passed by this Court in BLAPL No.9812 of 2019 and he has already undergone more than 3 (three) years of sentence after his conviction vide the impugned judgment dated 28.10.2022, considering the nature of allegation and the materials available on record, this Court is inclined to direct for release of the appellant on bail by keeping the sentence under suspension on such terms and conditions as deem fit and proper by the learned Court in seisin.

In addition to the terms and conditions to be imposed, this Court observe that appellant shall not involve himself in similar nature of offence and involvement in any manner will entail cancellation of the bail.
7. I.A. stands disposed of.
(Biraja Prasanna Satapathy) Judge 1.
Heard.
There shall be stay of realization of fine till disposal of the appeal.
3. I.A. stands disposed of.
(Biraja Prasanna Satapathy) Judge Basudev
